title: Intervention records with a point-key frequency cap
action: Plan Phase 2, first half (per c80debd7): interventions are FILE RECORDS with frequency-cap state. Extend the supervisor verb group: `bee supervisor record` gains --kind intervention, which REQUIRES --target-session, a --point-key (a stable slug naming the point being touched), and --question (an open question, at most 2 sentences — refuse longer). Frequency cap per c80debd7: the SECOND record for the same (target_session, point_key) is refused as a plain intervention and must be recorded with --kind escalation instead (same fields; the refusal names this remedy) — never repeat the same point. Add `bee supervisor pending --target-session <id> --json` listing undelivered intervention/escalation rows, and `bee supervisor mark-delivered --id <row-id>` stamping delivered_at (rows get a stable id). Keep observation|silence behavior byte-identical. Follow the existing validation-before-write seam; extend the same tests file: cap fires on second same-point record; escalation accepted; pending lists only undelivered; mark-delivered stamps and is idempotent-refusing on unknown id. Regen deferred to the wave barrier.

truths: a second intervention on the same (target_session, point_key) is refused naming --kind escalation as the remedy
pending lists only undelivered rows for the named session

artifacts.substantive: intervention/escalation kinds, point-key cap, pending + mark-delivered verbs, validated before write

key_links: dispatcher routes supervisor pending and supervisor mark-delivered
prohibitions: no hand-written .bee files outside the supervisor store

trace.outcome: Intervention/escalation mailbox with a point-key frequency cap, plus pending and mark-delivered verbs
deviations: Interventions went into their own store .bee/supervisor/interventions.jsonl instead of the observation log — an intervention is stamped delivered while an observation is written once and never touched, and separate stores keep observation|silence behavior byte-identical — found a better route

KNOWN_KINDS stayed the two tick kinds and the mailbox kinds took their own const (ALL_KINDS is the union the refusal names) — herding::control_loop pins the shipped supervisor prompt to KNOWN_KINDS and that prompt file is outside this cell files — hit an unforeseen obstacle

supervisor.record registry required went from [kind, note] to [kind] — hooks/cli_shape.rs enforces required statically and cannot express note-only-for-observation, so leaving it would block every intervention record at the hook; the verb still refuses a missing note — the plan was wrong about a fact
Added a secret/control-token refusal on --question — that text is delivered into another session context, so it takes the same guard capture add puts on stored text — found a better route

The worker could not commit: the intake gate read the control root default record (phase idle) because the session was bound to no lane; the orchestrator bound the session, re-ran the verify green, and committed — hit an unforeseen obstacle
